title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to Integrated Border Management (IBM) in Bangladesh

description.narrative: Bangladesh¿s economy relies heavily on labour migration, with remittances constituting a major source of foreign exchange and supporting household consumption and poverty reduction. This underlines the importance of effective migration governance. However, existing policy, regulatory and operational frameworks are not yet fully aligned with international standards and good practices. Persistent gaps in recruitment oversight, protection of migrant workers¿ rights, and migration data systems constrain the country¿s ability to ensure safe, orderly and regular migration and to maximize development benefits. These shortcomings also contribute to continued irregular migration, including towards the EU, highlighting the need for more coherent migration and border management systems.Bangladesh faces significant challenges in border management amid sustained migratory pressures, including irregular movements, document and identity fraud, and risks of trafficking in human beings and smuggling of migrants. These are compounded by complex land and maritime borders and the protracted Rohingya displacement situation. While core functions are in place, weaknesses in inter-agency coordination, risk analysis and systematic checks limit the capacity of authorities to prevent irregular movements and detect cross-border crime effectively.Building on previous support from the European Union, notably through the Integrated Border Management (IBM) in the Silk Routes Countries project and complementary assistance from the Republic of Poland, the proposed action will support the development of a coherent, nationally owned and sustainable (IBM) framework. It will start with a gap and needs assessment to inform a sequenced reform approach. It will then support the development of a National IBM Strategy and Action Plan, alongside strengthened governance and coordination mechanisms. Operational support will focus on standardising procedures, introducing phased digital reporting and alert systems, and strengthening risk analysis capacities, including the gradual establishment of risk analysis functions, to enable intelligence-led border checks. Targeted investments in infrastructure and equipment at selected border crossing points will be complemented by strengthened training and professionalisation systems, including a national pool of trainers, ensuring the integration of an inclusive and a human rights-based approach. Implementation will follow a phased and prioritize approach, allowing the progressive roll-out of selected reforms and operational capacities over the 4 years implementation period, in line with available resources and institutional absorption capacities.The action contributes to SDG 10.7, SDG 5, and SDG 16, aligns with the Regional Multi annual Indicative Programme for Asia and the Pacific 2021¿2027 (Priority Area 3: Migration, Forced Displacement and Mobility), and supports the objectives of the Global Alliance to Counter Migrant Smuggling. It also reflects the external dimension of EU migration policy as set out in Regulation (EU) 2024/1351, in line with the division of competences between the Union and its Member States. Furthermore, the action will align also with the Country Level Implementation Plan of Bangladesh.
